name: Nottinghamshire
description: Nottinghamshire is a county in the East Midlands known for its association with the legend of Robin Hood, Sherwood Forest and the city of Nottingham. It combines a major urban centre with former coalfield communities, agricultural areas and historic market towns.

places.name: Ashfield
places.description: A former coal-mining district in Nottinghamshire, its towns like Hucknall still carrying the legacy of the pits, alongside associations with poet Lord Byron.

places.name: Bassetlaw
places.description: A district in Nottinghamshire around the market town of Retford, historically linked to the Pilgrim Fathers, several of whom came from villages in this area before sailing for America.

places.name: Broxtowe
places.description: A district in Nottinghamshire on the western edge of Nottingham city, including the town of Beeston and countryside associated with author D.H. Lawrence, who was born nearby.

places.name: Gedling
places.description: A district on Nottingham's eastern edge, largely suburban, taking its name from a former colliery village now redeveloped into a country park.

places.name: Mansfield
places.description: A former coal-mining town in Nottinghamshire, its identity long shaped by the pits, with the Sherwood Forest fringes lying nearby.

places.name: Newark and Sherwood
places.description: A district in Nottinghamshire covering the historic market town of Newark-on-Trent and the legendary Sherwood Forest, home of the Robin Hood legend.

places.name: Nottingham
places.description: A historic city famed for its Robin Hood legend, with a medieval castle, extensive cave network beneath the city, and a strong lace-making heritage.

places.name: Rushcliffe
places.description: An affluent suburban district south of Nottingham, covering West Bridgford and the National Water Sports Centre at Holme Pierrepont.
